review_candidates.title: Senior Systems and Network Engineer
review_candidates.description: Job Details About IonQ IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world's leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ's newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance . Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Location: This role is based at our College Park, MD office, with the option to work a few days a week remotely. Travel: Up to 15% Job ID: 1741 The Role IonQ is building quantum computers at College Park, and the infrastructure underneath that work is a crucial component. A misconfigured VLAN or a failed provisioning job can stop a calibration run or delay a system build. We are looking for a Senior Systems and Network Engineer to own the classical infrastructure layer that directly supports quantum hardware builds and operation at our College Park site. This means provisioning the servers and system heads that control quantum hardware, building and maintaining the lab and datacenter networking those systems run on, and integrating the cameras, laser control systems, and other bespoke scientific hardware that make a quantum system work. This is lab-grade systems and network engineering: closer to research computing at a national facility than to corporate IT. You will spend your time with real hardware, real cabling, and real failure modes, and automation of infrastructure to help us continue to scale. Responsibilities Provision Linux servers and system heads for quantum hardware builds, including PXE boot, OS installation, and automated configuration Build and maintain infrastructure-as-code for server and network provisioning (Ansible, Kickstart, Foreman, Packer, Terraform, or equivalent), so systems are reproducible rather than hand-tuned Design, configure, and troubleshoot networking for lab and datacenter environments: VLANs, managed switches, firewalls, and structured cabling Integrate non-standard scientific and lab hardware into the compute environment, including cameras, laser control systems, and custom device drivers Use IPMI/BMC and other out-of-band tooling to manage a growing fleet of servers without physical intervention on every failure Define and document handoff criteria for when a system is ready to pass to the teams running experiments on it Diagnose and resolve infrastructure issues that are actively blocking a hardware build or an experimental run, and treat that urgency accordingly Partner with software, DevOps, and hardware engineering teams to understand what a new system needs before it arrives Write runbooks and documentation so that provisioning knowledge lives in a repo, not in one person's head Requirements 6+ years of experience in systems, network, or infrastructure engineering, with real hands-on time provisioning servers, not just managing a team that did Hands-on experience configuring and troubleshooting switches, firewalls, routers, and on-prem servers in a production environment; this is not a design-and-delegate role Direct experience configuring VLANs and managed-switch environments, including diagnosing and resolving a network problem yourself, without escalating to a dedicated network team Experience building or rebuilding a provisioning workflow using infrastructure-as-code or automation tooling (Ansible, Salt, Kickstart, Foreman, Cobbler, Packer, or equivalent) Experience integrating non-standard or custom hardware into a compute environment: a scientific instrument, a specialist peripheral, or a device with a custom driver Working knowledge of IPMI/BMC and out-of-band server management Strong scripting ability in Python, Go, or an equivalent language Comfort operating in an environment where infrastructure failure directly blocks the work, and where the playbook for a new hardware generation is still being written Preferred Qualifications Experience at a company running significant on-prem compute infrastructure at scale (bare-metal cloud, colocation, high-density compute), where you managed a real fleet rather than a handful of machines Experience with Kubernetes or container orchestration in a bare-metal or hybrid environment Experience with configuration drift detection and enforcement, and can describe how you verified idempotency in a provisioning pipeline Familiarity with cloud networking (AWS, Azure, GCP) and hybrid on-prem/cloud environments Experience in a research, national lab, or scientific compute environment Prior exposure to quantum computing or another deep-tech hardware domain (not required; hands-on infrastructure experience matters far more than domain background) The approximate base salary range for this position is $126,887 - $166,127. The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site. Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment. review_candidates.description: Company Overview Milestone Technologies is a global IT managed services firm that partners with organizations to scale their technology, infrastructure and services to drive specific business outcomes such as digital transformation, innovation, and operational agility. Milestone is focused on building an employee-first, performance-based culture and for over 25 years, we have a demonstrated history of supporting category-defining enterprise clients that are growing ahead of the market. The company specializes in providing solutions across Application Services and Consulting, Digital Product Engineering, Digital Workplace Services, Private Cloud Services, AI/Automation, and ServiceNow. Milestone culture is built to provide a collaborative, inclusive environment that supports employees and empowers them to reach their full potential. Our seasoned professionals deliver services based on Milestone’s best practices and service delivery framework. By leveraging our vast knowledge base to execute initiatives, we deliver both short-term and long-term value to our clients and apply continuous service improvement to deliver transformational benefits to IT. With Intelligent Automation, Milestone helps businesses further accelerate their IT transformation. Job Overview Radio over IP (RoIP) Infrastructure Admin Location: [San Francisco, CA / Seattle, WA / New York, NY / Remote] Reports To: [Security Technology Lead] Travel: [Up to 25%] About the Role: As part of client’s Global Safety, Intelligence, and Security (GSIS) team, the RoIP Infrastructure Admin will own the design, deployment, and ongoing operation of client’s radio communications environment across a rapidly expanding global office portfolio. Our security, facilities, and operations teams need to talk to one another reliably — within a building, across a campus, and between sites — and this role exists to make that possible without depending on VPN tunneling between locations. You’ll architect a tiered environment that fits each site to the right solution. Larger corporate offices need full radio-over-IP infrastructure: repeaters, antenna systems, FCC licensing, RoIP gateways, and fleets of handheld radios. Smaller offices and leased spaces, where dedicated radio infrastructure doesn’t make financial sense, need WiFi and cellular push-to-talk devices that feel like part of the same system. Tying it all together is a SaaS interconnect platform that links every site into a single, secure talkgroup environment. This is a build-and-run role. You’ll design and deploy radio infrastructure as new sites open, define the standards and playbooks that integrators execute against, maintain the environment once it’s live, and dispatch service engineers when equipment needs repair. You’ll work closely with Networking, IT Infrastructure, InfoSec, Facilities, and Project Management to make sure radio is treated as a first-class part of every site build. Your work will directly determine whether client’s teams can communicate reliably as the company grows from dozens of locations to a global enterprise footprint. Responsibilities: • Own the end-to-end architecture for client’s radio-over-IP (RoIP) communications environment, designing a network that connects corporate offices, hubs, and leased spaces over the public internet without relying on VPN tunneling • Design and deploy full RoIP radio infrastructure at larger corporate offices, including repeaters, antenna systems and in-building coverage, RoIP gateways, dispatch consoles, and handheld radio fleets • Specify, procure, and manage WiFi and cellular (push-to-talk over cellular) radio solutions for smaller offices and leased spaces where dedicated radio infrastructure is not financially justified, ensuring a consistent user experience across both deployment models • Select, implement, and administer the SaaS interconnect platform that links all sites into a single talkgroup environment, including tenant configuration, talkgroup and user provisioning, role-based access, encryption, and integration with client’s identity stack • Perform RF coverage analysis and site surveys for new and existing locations, producing coverage maps, link budgets, and antenna placement designs that meet operational coverage requirements • Obtain and maintain FCC Part 90 licenses for US sites and coordinate equivalent spectrum authorizations with international regulators (e.g., Ofcom, ComReg) as client’s footprint grows, including frequency coordination, renewals, and modifications • Define the network prerequisites for RoIP traffic — firewall rules, QoS, NAT traversal, bandwidth, and PoE — and partner with Networking, IT Infrastructure, and InfoSec to ensure every site meets them before go-live • Design and deploy radio infrastructure as part of the standard new-site opening process, working alongside Facilities, Project Management, and Security Technology to sequence radio work with construction, network, and security system installation • Build deployment playbooks, configuration baselines, radio codeplugs, and handoff documentation so that integrators and service partners can execute installations and repairs consistently across all sites • Maintain the deployed environment: monitor repeater, gateway, and SaaS platform health, manage firmware and software updates, track license and subscription renewals, and manage spares and handheld lifecycle • Act as the escalation point for radio service issues, triaging faults remotely and dispatching service engineers or vendor partners when equipment requires on-site repair, then verifying restoration • Manage radio vendors, integrators, and service contracts, holding partners to SLAs and evaluating new hardware and platforms for scalability, interoperability, and total cost of ownership • Support client’s security and emergency response programs by ensuring radio coverage, talkgroup design, and dispatch workflows meet the operational needs of on-site security, facilities, and event teams You may be a good fit if you: • Have 5+ years of hands-on experience designing, deploying, and maintaining land mobile radio (LMR) systems — DMR, P25, NXDN, or similar — in an enterprise, campus, venue, or public safety environment • Have designed and commissioned RoIP or interconnected radio systems that link geographically distributed sites over IP, and understand the trade-offs between conventional, trunked, and IP-linked architectures • Are fluent in RF fundamentals: coverage modeling, site surveys, antenna selection and placement, link budgets, interference mitigation, and in-building coverage solutions such as bi-directional amplifiers or distributed antenna systems • Have owned FCC Part 90 licensing from application through renewal, including frequency coordination and working with a frequency coordinator • Have deployed and supported push-to-talk-over-cellular or WiFi-based radio solutions and understand where they are the right tool versus dedicated radio infrastructure • Have strong IP networking knowledge — VLANs, QoS, NAT, firewalls, PoE, and multicast/unicast audio transport — and can articulate RoIP requirements to network and security engineers • Have managed a fleet of handheld radios at scale, including codeplug development, programming, accessory standards, battery lifecycle, and user training • Have built standards, playbooks, and documentation that allowed integrators and field technicians to execute against your designs without ambiguity • Have experience managing vendors and service contracts and coordinating field dispatch for break-fix repairs • Are comfortable with travel to sites for surveys, commissioning, and major service events Strong candidates may also have: • Hold an FCC General Radiotelephone Operator License (GROL) or equivalent, and/or manufacturer certifications from Motorola Solutions, Kenwood, Hytera, Tait, or L3Harris • Have experience with RoIP gateway and interconnect platforms such as JPS, Omnitronics, Zetron, Motorola WAVE PTX, or comparable SaaS PTT services • Have coordinated spectrum licensing outside the United States, or have deployed radio in a multinational corporate environment • Have integrated radio systems with dispatch, alarm monitoring, or physical security platforms (e.g., Genetec, SureView) • Hold networking or wireless certifications such as CCNA or CWNA, or project certifications such as PMP Compensation Estimated Pay Range: 156K-195K/year Exact compensation and offers of employment are dependent on circumstances of each case and will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, licenses or certifications, and location. review_candidates.description: About the Role We’re looking for someone to be our point person and incident commander at night — the hours our platform runs but Jester and the daytime team aren’t on. Our platform (Autopilot) helps 2,000+ dental labs worldwide get their cases booked correctly within 15 minutes of arrival, every time, so when something breaks overnight, someone has to be ready with a fast, safe fix immediately — not by morning. This is an individual contributor role, not a people-management position. You won’t have direct reports. What you will have is real responsibility: you’re the one who owns incident response at night, and you make sure the same process and communication standard that runs during the day holds up just as well at 2am. You’ll also train one Application Support team member to be your trusted backup at night — someone you can delegate real tasks to, not just someone shadowing you. What You’ll Own Incident command at night. When something breaks overnight, you declare it, triage it, and drive it to resolution — the same triage-first standard used during the day, applied consistently after hours. Platform monitoring, day and night. Watch the health of every module and catch problems early, whatever the hour. Cross-shift consistency. Make sure the process, tools, and communication flow used at night match what’s used during the day — no gaps, no separate “night version” of how things get handled. Training your night backup. Work with Jester to identify one Application Support team member as your trained backup for night coverage. Teach them to run real triage and delegate real tasks to them — not just observation. A close partnership with DevOps. Work directly with Jester and his team on keeping infrastructure stable and building better tools to catch problems automatically. Knowing when — and when not — to escalate further. Most problems get fixed at your level. For the rare cases that genuinely need more, you know exactly who to call and how. What Success Looks Like The platform stays healthy well over 99% of the time, day and night. Night incidents are handled fast and correctly — Jester never has to be pulled in personally to cover a night incident. Your trained backup can run night triage confidently on their own when needed. The daytime team never has to “catch up” on what happened overnight — communication is seamless across the shift change. What We’re Looking For Experience as an individual contributor in a technical support or incident response role — SaaS, platform operations, or similar. Comfortable owning a decision under pressure, alone, without a manager to check with in the moment. Able and willing to be the primary owner of incidents at night — this is the core of the role, not an occasional ask. Some hands-on comfort with basics like service restarts, log review, and ticketing systems (we use Jira). Deep DevOps expertise is not required — that’s Jester’s team; you need to know enough to apply a safe first fix and know when to hand off. Able to teach and delegate to a peer effectively, even without formal management authority. Clear, calm communicator — you’ll be updating customer-facing teams during live incidents. How We’ll Set You Up to Succeed The first 90 days follow a structured ramp: you’ll spend real time learning the platform and the team before you’re expected to run night incidents solo, then build up to full independent night ownership — including a trained backup — by the end of your first month. Full details are in the accompanying 90-Day Plan.

[NYSE: IONQ] is the world's leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ's newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance . Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Location: This role is based at our College Park, MD office, with the option to work a few days a week remotely. Travel: Up to 15% Job ID: 1741 The Role IonQ is building quantum computers at College Park, and the infrastructure underneath that work is a crucial component. A misconfigured VLAN or a failed provisioning job can stop a calibration run or delay a system build. We are looking for a Senior Systems and Network Engineer to own the classical infrastructure layer that directly supports quantum hardware builds and operation at our College Park site. This means provisioning the servers and system heads that control quantum hardware, building and maintaining the lab and datacenter networking those systems run on, and integrating the cameras, laser control systems, and other bespoke scientific hardware that make a quantum system work. By leveraging our vast knowledge base to execute initiatives, we deliver both short-term and long-term value to our clients and apply continuous service improvement to deliver transformational benefits to IT. With Intelligent Automation, Milestone helps businesses further accelerate their IT transformation. Job Overview Radio over IP (RoIP) Infrastructure Admin Location: [San Francisco, CA / Seattle, WA / New York, NY / Remote] Reports To: [Security Technology Lead] Travel: [Up to 25%] About the Role: As part of client’s Global Safety, Intelligence, and Security (GSIS) team, the RoIP Infrastructure Admin will own the design, deployment, and ongoing operation of client’s radio communications environment across a rapidly expanding global office portfolio. Our security, facilities, and operations teams need to talk to one another reliably — within a building, across a campus, and between sites — and this role exists to make that possible without depending on VPN tunneling between locations. You’ll architect a tiered environment that fits each site to the right solution. Larger corporate offices need full radio-over-IP infrastructure: repeaters, antenna systems, FCC licensing, RoIP gateways, and fleets of handheld radios. Smaller offices and leased spaces, where dedicated radio infrastructure doesn’t make financial sense, need WiFi and cellular push-to-talk devices that feel like part of the same system. Tying it all together is a SaaS interconnect platform that links every site into a single, secure talkgroup environment. This is a build-and-run role. You’ll design and deploy radio infrastructure as new sites open, define the standards and playbooks that integrators execute against, maintain the environment once it’s live, and dispatch service engineers when equipment needs repair. You’ll work closely with Networking, IT Infrastructure, InfoSec, Facilities, and Project Management to make sure radio is treated as a first-class part of every site build. Your work will directly determine whether client’s teams can communicate reliably as the company grows from dozens of locations to a global enterprise footprint. Responsibilities: • Own the end-to-end architecture for client’s radio-over-IP (RoIP) communications environment, designing a network that connects corporate offices, hubs, and leased spaces over the public internet without relying on VPN tunneling • Design and deploy full RoIP radio infrastructure at larger corporate offices, including repeaters, antenna systems and in-building coverage, RoIP gateways, dispatch consoles, and handheld radio fleets • Specify, procure, and manage WiFi and cellular (push-to-talk over cellular) radio solutions for smaller offices and leased spaces where dedicated radio infrastructure is not financially justified, ensuring a consistent user experience across both deployment models • Select, implement, and administer the SaaS interconnect platform that links all sites into a single talkgroup environment, including tenant configuration, talkgroup and user provisioning, role-based access, encryption, and integration with client’s identity stack • Perform RF coverage analysis and site surveys for new and existing locations, producing coverage maps, link budgets, and antenna placement designs that meet operational coverage requirements • Obtain and maintain FCC Part 90 licenses for US sites and coordinate equivalent spectrum authorizations with international regulators (e.g., Ofcom, ComReg) as client’s footprint grows, including frequency coordination, renewals, and modifications • Define the network prerequisites for RoIP traffic — firewall rules, QoS, NAT traversal, bandwidth, and PoE — and partner with Networking, IT Infrastructure, and InfoSec to ensure every site meets them before go-live • Design and deploy radio infrastructure as part of the standard new-site opening process, working alongside Facilities, Project Management, and Security Technology to sequence radio work with construction, network, and security system installation • Build deployment playbooks, configuration baselines, radio codeplugs, and handoff documentation so that integrators and service partners can execute installations and repairs consistently across all sites • Maintain the deployed environment: monitor repeater, gateway, and SaaS platform health, manage firmware and software updates, track license and subscription renewals, and manage spares and handheld lifecycle • Act as the escalation point for radio service issues, triaging faults remotely and dispatching service engineers or vendor partners when equipment requires on-site repair, then verifying restoration • Manage radio vendors, integrators, and service contracts, holding partners to SLAs and evaluating new hardware and platforms for scalability, interoperability, and total cost of ownership • Support client’s security and emergency response programs by ensuring radio coverage, talkgroup design, and dispatch workflows meet the operational needs of on-site security, facilities, and event teams You may be a good fit if you: • Have 5+ years of hands-on experience designing, deploying, and maintaining land mobile radio (LMR) systems — DMR, P25, NXDN, or similar — in an enterprise, campus, venue, or public safety environment • Have designed and commissioned RoIP or interconnected radio systems that link geographically distributed sites over IP, and understand the trade-offs between conventional, trunked, and IP-linked architectures • Are fluent in RF fundamentals: coverage modeling, site surveys, antenna selection and placement, link budgets, interference mitigation, and in-building coverage solutions such as bi-directional amplifiers or distributed antenna systems • Have owned FCC Part 90 licensing from application through renewal, including frequency coordination and working with a frequency coordinator • Have deployed and supported push-to-talk-over-cellular or WiFi-based radio solutions and understand where they are the right tool versus dedicated radio infrastructure • Have strong IP networking knowledge — VLANs, QoS, NAT, firewalls, PoE, and multicast/unicast audio transport — and can articulate RoIP requirements to network and security engineers • Have managed a fleet of handheld radios at scale, including codeplug development, programming, accessory standards, battery lifecycle, and user training • Have built standards, playbooks, and documentation that allowed integrators and field technicians to execute against your designs without ambiguity • Have experience managing vendors and service contracts and coordinating field dispatch for break-fix repairs • Are comfortable with travel to sites for surveys, commissioning, and major service events Strong candidates may also have: • Hold an FCC General Radiotelephone Operator License (GROL) or equivalent, and/or manufacturer certifications from Motorola Solutions, Kenwood, Hytera, Tait, or L3Harris • Have experience with RoIP gateway and interconnect platforms such as JPS, Omnitronics, Zetron, Motorola WAVE PTX, or comparable SaaS PTT services • Have coordinated spectrum licensing outside the United States, or have deployed radio in a multinational corporate environment • Have integrated radio systems with dispatch, alarm monitoring, or physical security platforms (e.g., Genetec, SureView) • Hold networking or wireless certifications such as CCNA or CWNA, or project certifications such as PMP Compensation Estimated Pay certifications, and location. new_matches.description: About the Role We’re looking for someone to be our point person and incident commander at night — the hours our platform runs but Jester and the daytime team aren’t on. Our platform (Autopilot) helps 2,000+ dental labs worldwide get their cases booked correctly within 15 minutes of arrival, every time, so when something breaks overnight, someone has to be ready with a fast, safe fix immediately — not by morning. This is an individual contributor role, not a people-management position. You won’t have direct reports. What you will have is real responsibility: you’re the one who owns incident response at night, and you make sure the same process and communication standard that runs during the day holds up just as well at 2am. You’ll also train one Application Support team member to be your trusted backup at night — someone you can delegate real tasks to, not just someone shadowing you. What You’ll Own Incident command at night. When something breaks overnight, you declare it, triage it, and drive it to resolution — the same triage-first standard used during the day, applied consistently after hours. Platform monitoring, day and night. Watch the health of every module and catch problems early, whatever the hour. Cross-shift consistency. Make sure the process, tools, and communication flow used at night match what’s used during the day — no gaps, no separate “night version” of how things get handled. Training your night backup. Work with Jester to identify one Application Support team member as your trained backup for night coverage. Teach them to run real triage and delegate real tasks to them — not just observation. A close partnership with DevOps. Work directly with Jester and his team on keeping infrastructure stable and building better tools to catch problems automatically. Knowing when — and when not — to escalate further. Most problems get fixed at your level. For the rare cases that genuinely need more, you know exactly who to call and how. What Success Looks Like The platform stays healthy well over 99% of the time, day and night. Night incidents are handled fast and correctly — Jester never has to be pulled in personally to cover a night incident. Your trained backup can run night triage confidently on their own when needed. The daytime team never has to “catch up” on what happened overnight — communication is seamless across the shift change. What We’re Looking For Experience as an individual contributor in a technical support or incident response role — SaaS, platform operations, or similar. Comfortable owning a decision under pressure, alone, without a manager to check with in the moment. Able and willing to be the primary owner of incidents at night — this is the core of the role, not an occasional ask. Some hands-on comfort with basics like service restarts, log review, and ticketing systems (we use Jira). Deep DevOps expertise is not required — that’s Jester’s team; you need to know enough to apply a safe first fix and know when to hand off. Able to teach and delegate to a peer effectively, even without formal management authority. Clear, calm communicator — you’ll be updating customer-facing teams during live incidents. How We’ll Set You Up to Succeed The first 90 days follow a structured ramp: you’ll spend real time learning the platform and the team before you’re expected to run night incidents solo, then build up to full independent night ownership — including a trained backup — by the end of your first month. Full details are in the accompanying 90-Day Plan.
